justification: Standard: real behaviour change to a live, deployed API endpoint's failure path (500 instead of a fake 200 'submitted'). Not Critical because the blast radius is narrow (no frontend caller for this endpoint was found anywhere in this repo, so today's real-world traffic is unproven) and the change is contained to one except block in one function, already regression-tested by forcing it to fail against the pre-fix code (git stash) and confirming the new tests go red.

pre_impl.existing_data: drawdown_verify_audits table -- confirmed live 2026-09-04 to NOT exist in production (DQ-91). This fix does not create it (a production DDL write was blocked by the session's own auto-mode classifier and needs explicit user approval, see PR body) -- it only stops the API from lying about the outcome while the table is still missing.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: None new. The pre-existing code already assumed _insert_audit could fail (it had a try/except); this fix only changes what happens on that already-anticipated failure.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every new request from merge onward. No historical rows are affected -- there is nothing to backfill, since the table has never held any rows.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- no new external source call added.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A -- no frontend caller found for this endpoint in this repo.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: caller receives 200 'submitted' with a non-functional fallback ID (job_name, not a UUID -- polling GET /pipeline/drawdown-verify/{job_id} with it would itself fail on invalid UUID syntax) while the audit record silently does not exist. After: caller receives 500 with an explicit 'has NOT been recorded' message and the hyp3_job_name for manual reconciliation, matching the existing HyP3-submission-failure pattern three lines above in the same function.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The fix in services/drawdown_verify.py is reverted while the new tests are kept -- proven, not assumed, by actually running git stash push -- services/drawdown_verify.py, re-running the same pytest command, then git stash pop to restore the fix.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 2 of 4 tests went RED against the pre-fix code: test_audit_insert_failure_raises_500_not_a_fake_success and test_audit_insert_failure_response_carries_the_hyp3_job_name_for_reconciliation both printed 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class fastapi.exceptions.HTTPException>', with the captured log line 'ERROR services.drawdown_verify:drawdown_verify.py:516 Audit insert failed for loan loan-123' showing the old code swallowing the exception exactly as expected. Result line: '2 failed, 2 passed in 0.67s' -- the 2 that stayed green (test_audit_insert_success_still_returns_submitted, test_hyp3_submission_failure_is_unchanged_by_this_fix) are unrelated to this fix and correctly unaffected.

functions.name: submit_drawdown_verify
functions.if_none: N/A -- request is a validated pydantic model, FastAPI rejects a malformed body before this function runs

values.nullable: no -- previously silently set to job_name (a non-UUID string) on failure; now the function never reaches this line on failure, it raises instead
values.if_missing: Caller gets HTTPException 500 before a response body is ever constructed

break_it.scenario: Audit insert fails (table missing, connection drop, constraint violation) after the HyP3 job has already been submitted.
break_it.what_happens: Before: caller told 'submitted', given a job_id that cannot be polled, audit record permanently missing with nothing surfaced. After: caller gets a 500 naming the failure and the hyp3_job_name for manual reconciliation; the HyP3 job itself is NOT cancelled (documented in the new code comment) so it is not silently wasted, just not auto-tracked.
break_it.how: services/drawdown_verify.py:504-534, raise HTTPException(500, ...) replaces the silent log-and-continue
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_drawdown_verify_audit_failclosed.py -v -- forced against the pre-fix code via git stash to confirm it actually fails without the fix (not just exercises the code)

break_it.scenario: This fix accidentally also breaks the SUCCESS path or the unrelated HyP3-submission failure path.
break_it.what_happens: Would silently regress a working flow while fixing a broken one.
break_it.how: test_audit_insert_success_still_returns_submitted and test_hyp3_submission_failure_is_unchanged_by_this_fix pin both, unaffected by this diff

break_it.scenario: Because drawdown_verify_audits still does not exist in production (the migration was NOT run this session, see post_merge below), every real call to this endpoint will now return 500 instead of the previous fake 200 -- a 0% to 100% visible-failure-rate jump for any existing caller, the moment this merges.
break_it.what_happens: If anything IS calling this endpoint today (unproven either way -- no caller was found in this repo, but that does not rule out an external caller), it goes from silently-broken-but-200 to loudly-broken-500 immediately on merge, before the table exists to fix the root cause.
break_it.how: Not mitigated by this PR -- this is the correct and intended direction (loud failure over silent lie) but it is a real, immediate behaviour change that should not be merged without the person merging knowing it. The actual fix (create the table) is still blocked pending explicit approval to run migrations/033_drawdown_verify_audits.sql against production.
break_it.repro: N/A -- this is a deployed-behaviour consequence, not something a local test reproduces

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- the underlying gap (drawdown_verify_audits does not exist) is NOT fixed by this PR. Running migrations/033_drawdown_verify_audits.sql against production was attempted this session and blocked by the auto-mode classifier as a production DDL write requiring explicit approval. This PR only stops the endpoint from lying about the outcome while that table is still missing -- DQ-91 stays 'open' until the migration is actually run.
